output.title: Know the demo limit before you automate
output.body:
If you have tried ChatGPT but have not connected it to a real workflow, the first question is not whether AI can answer a prompt. It is whether it fits one recurring task in your business without creating a second manual job around it. That is the useful boundary demo limits expose.

For a small business, the best candidate is usually a frequent, repeatable workflow with a measurable outcome, already living in English, email, documents, or SaaS tools. The 8–10 hours a week example is only a persona frame: repeated customer questions, neglected leads, or manual invoice work. It is not a market claim.

Our self-built demos show the mechanism, but only inside their limits. The knowledge assistant works end to end locally on synthetic Acme Shop data and approved documents; the deployed public route is locked. The accounts-payable demo uses synthetic data for a fictional manufacturer, can block duplicate invoices, and requires human approval for risky steps. Neither demo proves OCR, billing, multi-user operation, or autonomous money movement. Computers are still bad at hearing “trust me” and wiring up payments.

So the practical next step is simple: look at one recurring workflow and ask three things. Is the output measurable? Is the data already digital? Can a person approve the risky part? If the answer is unclear, the workflow is probably not ready. If it is clear, that is the boundary worth testing.
